description: A single rendered table, with no axes, plot, micrograph, scale bar or colour legend. The columns are headed Steel, C, Mn, Al, Fe and Density (g/cm³); numeric compositions are printed without an explicit unit in the header, and Fe is given as "Bal." in every row. Thirteen alloys are listed in three series: Fe30Mn 11Al(x)C (C-0.6, C-1.0, C-1.2, C-1.5) with varying C; Fe(x)Mn 11Al1C (Mn-20, Mn-25, Mn-30, Mn-35) with varying Mn; and Fe30Mn (x)Al1C (Al-6, Al-8, Al-10, Al-11, Al-12) with varying Al. Within series 1, C rises from 0.63 to 1.52 while density falls from 6.65 to 6.56 g/cm³; within series 2, Mn rises from 19.09 to 34.23 while density falls from 6.69 to 6.53 g/cm³; within series 3, Al rises from 5.98 to 12.04 while density falls from 7.12 to 6.52 g/cm³. The table therefore records the measured chemistries of the three alloy series and demonstrates that raising C, Mn or Al content progressively lowers the density of the steel.

observations.observation: The figure is a single chemical-composition table with the column headers Steel, C, Mn, Al, Fe and Density (g/cm³); no units are printed for the C, Mn and Al columns.

Thirteen alloys are tabulated, grouped into three series: Fe30Mn 11Al(x)C (C-0.6, C-1.0, C-1.2, C-1.5), Fe(x)Mn 11Al1C (Mn-20, Mn-25, Mn-30, Mn-35) and Fe30Mn (x)Al1C (Al-6, Al-8, Al-10, Al-11, Al-12).
Row C-0.6 reads C 0.63, Mn 30.10, Al 11.11, Fe Bal., Density 6.65 g/cm³; row C-1.5 reads C 1.52, Mn 29.67, Al 11.21, Fe Bal., Density 6.56 g/cm³.
Row Mn-20 reads C 1.01, Mn 19.09, Al 10.87, Density 6.69 g/cm³; row Mn-35 reads C 1.00, Mn 34.23, Al 11.10, Density 6.53 g/cm³.
Row Al-6 reads C 0.99, Mn 29.48, Al 5.98, Density 7.12 g/cm³; row Al-12 reads C 1.02, Mn 30.47, Al 12.04, Density 6.52 g/cm³.
Within the Fe30Mn 11Al(x)C series density decreases monotonically from 6.65 g/cm³ (C-0.6) to 6.56 g/cm³ (C-1.5) as C content increases.
Within the Fe(x)Mn 11Al1C series density decreases monotonically from 6.69 g/cm³ (Mn-20) to 6.53 g/cm³ (Mn-35) as Mn content increases.

Within the Fe30Mn (x)Al1C series density decreases monotonically from 7.12 g/cm³ (Al-6) to 6.52 g/cm³ (Al-12) as Al content increases; Al-6 is the densest alloy and Al-12 the least dense in the whole table.
Iron is reported as 'Bal.' (balance) in every one of the thirteen rows.
The caption identifies the tabulated material as FeMnAlC fabricated by the vacuum induction melting method.
The citing abstract states the series covers C from 0.6 to 1.5%, Mn from 20 to 35% and Al from 6.0 to 12.0%, matching the tabulated ranges (C 0.63-1.52, Mn 19.09-34.23, Al 5.98-12.04).
The tabulated densities span 6.52 to 7.12 g/cm³ over the thirteen alloys, i.e. all are lighter than pure iron-based steel, consistent with the low-density steel designation.

subfigures.description: Single chemical-composition table of Fe–Mn–Al–C low-density steels, with columns Steel, C, Mn, Al, Fe and Density (g/cm³) and 13 data rows in three composition series (Fe30Mn 11Al(x)C; Fe(x)Mn 11Al1C; Fe30Mn (x)Al1C). Fe is 'Bal.' in all rows.
